title: Most Pieces That Sort Independently
statement:
You get an array arr of length n holding each of the numbers 0, 1, …, n − 1 exactly once.

Cut it into contiguous pieces, sort each piece on its own, and glue the pieces back together in their original order. The glued result must be fully sorted. Return the largest number of pieces you can cut it into.

examples.why: Pieces [1, 0] | [2] | [4, 3] sort to [0, 1] [2] [3, 4]. Only 2 is already in place, so counting fixed points (1) is wrong.
The 3 must travel to the end, so every element is in the same piece as it.
Already sorted: every element can be its own piece.

constraints: arr is a permutation of 0 … n − 1
hints: When can you close a piece right after position i?
The sorted array has the values 0 … i in the first i + 1 slots. So the prefix arr[0..i] must contain exactly those values.
Since the values are distinct and between 0 and n − 1, that is the same as: the largest value in arr[0..i] equals i.

explain.intuition:
A cut after position i is allowed exactly when the left part already holds the values that belong there, 0 … i. Pieces never exchange elements, so anything in the left part must end up in the left part.

With a permutation, "the first i + 1 values are exactly 0 … i" is the same as "the maximum of the prefix is i": i + 1 distinct non-negative values whose maximum is i can only be 0 … i. Every allowed cut can be made at once, so count the positions where the running maximum equals the index.
steps: Keep a running maximum mx, starting at −1, and pieces = 0.
For each index i, set mx = max(mx, arr[i]).
If mx === i, a piece can end here: increment pieces.
pitfalls: Counting positions where arr[i] === i. In [1, 0, 2, 4, 3] that gives 1, but the answer is 3.
Comparing the running maximum to i + 1 or checking it before including arr[i]: an off-by-one that closes pieces one step early.

solutions.title: Compare each prefix with its sorted version
solutions.idea: A cut after i works when the sorted prefix equals 0 … i. Sort every prefix to check.

solutions.title: Running maximum
solutions.idea: A piece can end at i exactly when the largest value seen so far is i.

followups: Values may now repeat and are not limited to 0 … n − 1. What condition replaces "max equals index"? (Compare prefix max with suffix min, or use a monotonic stack.)
Return the cut positions themselves, not just the count.
